c.tagline: Puglia's port capital, of a whitewashed old town, orecchiette, and ferries to the Balkans.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are white and metered, with a fixed fare of around €25 from the airport to the centre. Uber offers only its licensed taxi/black-car service in Bari (no UberX), so hailing at a rank or booking through Free Now or the itTaxi/appTaxi apps is the norm.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance; 113 reaches state police and 118 reaches medical emergencies directly.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the old town and around the station

hood_desc: The whitewashed medieval labyrinth on the peninsula, home to the Basilica di San Nicola, the Norman-Swabian Castle, and lanes where local women hand-roll orecchiette in their doorways; best for first-timers who want the sights and old-world atmosphere on their doorstep.

The elegant 19th-century grid laid out under Napoleon's brother-in-law Joachim Murat, centred on the pedestrian shopping street Via Sparano and Corso Cavour, with boutiques, cafes, and easy access to the seafront and station; the convenient, walkable base for most visitors.

A characterful residential quarter along the Lungomare seafront promenade east of the centre, mixing faded palazzi, local trattorias, and a slowly gentrifying creative edge; suits travellers wanting sea views and a lived-in feel.

A leafy, upscale residential district south of the centre with quiet streets, parks, and modern apartment blocks; calm and family-friendly, better suited to longer stays and those travelling with a car.
A gritty, multicultural neighbourhood just west of the station, packed with markets, cheap eats, and budget rooms; authentic and well-connected, appealing to travellers watching their wallet.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though many locals prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: AMTAB buses run roughly 5:30 AM to around 9:00-10:00 PM on most lines, with a reduced evening service; taxis and ride apps cover the late hours.
transit.note: Bari has no metro; AMTAB runs the city buses (including seafront routes and park-and-ride shuttles), while regional trains from Bari Centrale plus the Ferrotramviaria and FSE lines reach the airport and towns across Puglia. The compact centre and old town are easily walked.
transit.pay: A single AMTAB ticket is €1.00 (90 minutes) from tobacconists and newsstands, or €1.50 on board; a day pass is around €2.50. Validate on boarding, and contactless card payment is available on some lines.

bus: Bari Centrale coach terminal (Largo Sorrentino, Flixbus & intercity)

transit.m: Ferrotramviaria train (FM2) to Bari Centrale (~15 min)
AMTAB bus 16 to city centre (~25-35 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a cover charge (coperto) is usually on the bill, so rounding up or leaving a euro or two for good service is appreciated but not expected.

food.name: Orecchiette alle cime di rapa
food.desc: Hand-shaped little ears of durum pasta with bitter turnip tops, garlic, chilli, anchovy and Puglian olive oil. The defining Bari plate.

places.name: La Uascezze
places.note: Home-style old-city kitchen; the orecchiette is the reason to book, wine included in the set price.

places.name: Terranima
places.note: One of the city's most consistent versions in a warm, tiled dining room; broad Puglian menu.

places.name: Strada delle Orecchiette (Arco Basso)
places.note: The famous lane where nonnas shape pasta at street tables; buy fresh orecchiette to take home.

food.name: Focaccia barese
food.desc: Thick, olive-oil-soaked potato dough baked with cherry tomatoes and green olives, sold by weight and eaten standing up.

places.name: Panificio Fiore
places.note: The city benchmark; wood-oven focaccia sells out early, so arrive well before lunch.

places.name: Santa Rita bakery
places.note: Close runner-up, open from early morning until about 14:00 and popular with locals.

places.name: Panificio Fiore Bari Centro
places.note: Handy central bakery counter when the old-town queues are long; same by-the-slice format.

food.name: Panzerotti
food.desc: Half-moon fried dough pockets oozing tomato and mozzarella, the classic Bari snack eaten hot from a paper napkin.

places.name: Di Cosimo
places.note: Most-recommended panzerotti in town; queues build after 20:00, so go early evening.

places.name: Rosticceria Dirello
places.note: Reliable oven-fresh counter for panzerotti plus rustici and other fried Puglian snacks.

places.name: Bari Vecchia fry shops
places.note: Small friggitorie around the old town fry panzerotti to order through the evening.

food.name: Sgagliozze
food.desc: Deep-fried diamonds of polenta, salted and served in paper cones; pure Bari Vecchia street food sold from doorways at night.

places.name: Largo Albicocca stalls
places.note: The legendary sgagliozze corner; vendors set up each evening and the square fills with locals.

places.name: Maria delle Sgagliozze
places.note: The best-known doorway fryer, working the same spot for decades; cash only, tiny portions cheap.

places.name: Strada Vallisa evening stalls
places.note: More fryers along the old-town lanes doing sgagliozze and popizze after dark.

food.name: Tiella di riso, patate e cozze
food.desc: Layered oven bake of rice, potato and mussels with tomato, onion and pecorino; Bari's great Sunday one-dish meal.

places.name: Terranima
places.note: Does the tiella properly with local mussels; good place to try it alongside orecchiette.

places.name: La Uascezze
places.note: Home-cooking menu that rotates classic Bari bakes including the tiella.

places.name: Osteria delle Travi Il Buco
places.note: No-frills old-town osteria beloved for traditional Barese cooking and cheap house wine.

food.name: Crudo di mare (raw seafood)
food.desc: Sea urchins, raw prawns, octopus and allievi eaten straight off the boats at the harbour, with lemon and nothing else.

places.name: N'derr la lanz
places.note: The fishermen's raw-seafood stalls; morning-fresh urchins and octopus eaten standing at the quay.

places.name: Al Pescatore
places.note: Sit-down seafood standby by the castle for crudo platters if raw-at-the-dock feels too rough.

places.name: Mercato del Pesce
places.note: The covered fish market next to the port, best visited early for the day's landings.

food.name: Primitivo and Negroamaro wine
food.desc: Puglia's big-hearted reds from Gioia del Colle and the Salento, poured by the glass everywhere in Bari; ask for local rosato in summer.

places.name: Vini e Cucina
places.note: Historic no-frills trattoria where cheap regional wine comes with proper Barese plates.

places.name: Terranima
places.note: Well-chosen Puglian list with staff happy to explain Primitivo versus Negroamaro.

places.name: Osteria delle Travi Il Buco
places.note: Old-town room with house wine by the carafe and a loud, local crowd.

food.name: Caffe leccese
food.desc: Puglia's summer coffee: espresso poured over ice with almond milk, sweet, cold and reviving on a hot Adriatic afternoon.

places.name: Martinucci Laboratory
places.note: Salento pastry house with Bari outlets; textbook caffe leccese and pasticciotto pastries.

places.name: Via Sparano cafes
places.note: The main shopping street is lined with bars pouring caffe leccese all summer.

places.name: Bari Vecchia bar counters
places.note: Old-town bars will make it on request; cheapest way to try the almond-coffee combination.

landmarks: Basilica di San Nicola
An 11th-century Romanesque basilica holding the relics of St. Nicholas, drawing Catholic and Orthodox pilgrims to its luminous crypt.
Bari Vecchia (Old Town)
A labyrinth of whitewashed alleys, shrines, and laundry lines where daily life spills onto the streets between forty churches.
Castello Svevo (Swabian Castle)
Frederick II's massive moated fortress guarding the old town's edge, its ramparts and halls hosting exhibitions above Norman foundations.
Cattedrale di San Sabino
Bari's serene Romanesque cathedral, built over a Byzantine church whose mosaic floor still glimmers in the crypt below.
Strada delle Orecchiette (Via Arco Basso)
The famous alley where Barese women hand-roll orecchiette pasta on wooden boards outside their doorways, a living culinary tradition.
Lungomare Nazario Sauro
One of Italy's longest seafront promenades, a Liberty-era sweep of white balustrades made for passeggiata strolls at golden hour.
Piazza Mercantile and Piazza Ferrarese
Twin linked squares at the old town's gateway, buzzing with café tables around the medieval 'Column of Justice.'
Teatro Petruzzelli
Italy's fourth-largest theater, a crimson-and-gold opera house risen from a devastating 1991 fire to reclaim its cultural throne.
Teatro Margherita
A stilt-built Art Nouveau theater floating over the old harbor, reborn as a contemporary art space on the waterfront.
Pane e Pomodoro Beach
The city's cheerful urban beach, where Baresi swim within sight of the port, a short stroll from the center.

train.note: Bari has no international trains. Bari Centrale sits on the Adriatic line, with Trenitalia and Italo high-speed and Intercity trains to Bologna, Milan, Rome (~4h via the new fast link), Venice, and Turin, plus frequent regional services to Lecce, Brindisi, Foggia, and Barletta; FSE and Ferrotramviaria lines reach Matera, Taranto, and the airport.

bus.note: Long-distance coaches use the terminal beside Bari Centrale (Largo Sorrentino). Flixbus, Itabus, and Marino/Marozzi run domestic routes across Puglia and to Rome, Naples, and Florence, plus international links toward Eastern Europe.

ferry.note: The Port of Bari is a major Adriatic ferry hub. Regular car ferries sail to Greece (Igoumenitsa and Patras), Albania (Durres), and Montenegro (Bar), with seasonal links to Dubrovnik (Croatia); operators include Superfast, Ventouris, Grimaldi Lines, and Jadrolinija.

half.name: Alberobello
half.blurb: A town in Puglia's Itria Valley famous for its trulli, whitewashed conical-roofed stone houses unique to the region.

half.name: Polignano a Mare
half.blurb: A cliffside town built on limestone bluffs above the Adriatic, with a small beach tucked into a cove beneath the old center.

half.name: Matera
half.blurb: An ancient city built into a ravine, its cave dwellings and church interiors carved directly into the rock over thousands of years.

half.name: Castel del Monte
half.blurb: A 13th-century octagonal castle built by Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II atop a hill in Puglia, its geometric design still not fully explained.

half.name: Ostuni
half.blurb: A hill town known as the White City for its whitewashed old center, overlooking olive groves that stretch to the Adriatic coast.
